{{technical|date=June 2012}}
In [[mathematics]] and, in particular, [[differential geometry]] a '''circular surface''' is the image of a [[smooth function|map]] ''ƒ''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''I''&nbsp;&times;&nbsp;''S''<sup>1</sup>&nbsp;→&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>3</sup>, where ''I''&nbsp;⊂&nbsp;'''R''' is an [[open interval]] and ''S''<sup>1</sup> is the [[unit circle]], defined by

:<math> f(t,\theta) := \gamma(t) + r(t){\mathbf u}(t)\cos\theta + r(t){\mathbf v}(t)\sin\theta, \, </math>

where γ, '''u''', '''v''' : ''I'' → '''R'''<sup>3</sup> and ''r''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''I''&nbsp;→&nbsp;'''R'''<sub>>0</sub>, when {{nowrap|1 = '''R'''<sub>>0</sub> := { ''x'' &isin; '''R''' : ''x'' > 0 }.}} Moreover, it is usually assumed that '''u&nbsp;·&nbsp;u''' =&nbsp;'''v&nbsp;·&nbsp;v''' =&nbsp;1 and '''u · v''' = 0, where dot denotes the canonical [[scalar product]] on '''R'''<sup>3</sup>, i.e. '''u''' and '''v''' are [[unit length]] and mutually [[perpendicular]]. The map γ&nbsp;:&nbsp;''I''&nbsp;→&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>3</sup> is called the '''base curve''' for the circular surface and the two maps '''u''',&nbsp;'''v'''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''I''&nbsp;→&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>3</sup> are called the '''direction frame''' for the circular surface. For a fixed ''t''<sub>0</sub>&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''I'' the image of ''ƒ''(''t''<sub>0</sub>,&nbsp;''θ'') is called a '''generating [[circle]]''' of the circular surface.<ref>S. Izumiya, K. Saji, and N. Takeuchi, "Circular Surfaces", ''Advances in Geometry'', de Gruyter, Vol 7, 2007, 295&ndash;313.</ref>

Circular surfaces are an analogue of [[ruled surface]]s. In the case of circular surfaces the generators are circles; called the generating circles. In the case of ruled surface the generators are straight lines; called rulings.
